name: high-school-graduate
description: Core knowledge a high school graduate should have across math, science, English, social studies, civics, economics, health, and technology literacy. This is the base layer for all specialist training.

facts.fact: The order of operations (PEMDAS) is: Parentheses, Exponents, Multiplication and Division (left to right), Addition and Subtraction (left to right)
A prime number is a natural number greater than 1 that has exactly two factors: 1 and itself
The least common multiple (LCM) of two numbers is the smallest number that is a multiple of both
The greatest common factor (GCF) of two numbers is the largest number that divides both without remainder
A fraction represents a part of a whole, with a numerator on top and denominator on bottom
To add fractions with different denominators, find a common denominator first, then add the numerators
To convert a fraction to a percentage, divide the numerator by the denominator and multiply by 100
A decimal is another way to represent a fraction, using a decimal point to separate whole numbers from fractional parts
Ratios compare two quantities, while proportions state that two ratios are equal
Percent change is calculated as (new value - original value) / original value times 100
A variable is a symbol, usually a letter, that represents an unknown number in an equation
A linear equation forms a straight line when graphed and has the form y = mx + b where m is slope and b is y-intercept
The slope of a line is the change in y divided by the change in x (rise over run)
A quadratic equation has the form ax squared plus bx plus c equals zero, and its graph is a parabola
The quadratic formula is x equals negative b plus or minus the square root of b squared minus 4ac, all divided by 2a
The distributive property states that a times (b plus c) equals ab plus ac
Like terms are terms with the same variables raised to the same powers, and they can be combined by adding or subtracting coefficients
An inequality uses symbols like less than, greater than, less than or equal to, or greater than or equal to instead of an equals sign
A function is a relationship where each input has exactly one output
The domain of a function is the set of all possible input values, and the range is the set of all possible output values
Factoring is the process of breaking down an expression into simpler parts (factors) that multiply together to give the original expression
A system of linear equations can be solved by substitution, elimination, or graphing to find where the lines intersect
The sum of angles in any triangle is 180 degrees
The Pythagorean theorem states that in a right triangle, a squared plus b squared equals c squared, where c is the hypotenuse
The area of a rectangle is length times width
The area of a circle is pi times radius squared
The circumference of a circle is 2 times pi times radius, or pi times diameter
The volume of a rectangular prism is length times width times height
Parallel lines never intersect and are always the same distance apart
Perpendicular lines intersect at a 90 degree angle
Similar triangles have the same shape but possibly different sizes, with corresponding angles equal and sides proportional
A polygon is a closed shape with straight sides, and a regular polygon has all sides and angles equal
The angles on a straight line sum to 180 degrees
The sum of interior angles of an n-sided polygon is (n minus 2) times 180 degrees
The mean (average) of a data set is the sum of all values divided by the number of values
The median is the middle value when data is arranged in order
The mode is the value that appears most frequently in a data set
Range is the difference between the maximum and minimum values in a data set
Probability of an event is the number of favorable outcomes divided by the total number of possible outcomes
A bar graph uses rectangular bars to compare quantities, while a line graph shows trends over time
A pie chart shows parts of a whole as slices of a circle, with each slice proportional to its percentage
Standard deviation measures how spread out the data values are from the mean
Correlation measures the relationship between two variables, ranging from -1 to 1
A sample is a subset of a population used to make inferences about the whole population
The cell is the basic unit of life, and all living organisms are made of one or more cells
DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) carries the genetic instructions for the development and functioning of living organisms
Photosynthesis is the process by which plants use sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide to produce glucose and oxygen
Mitosis is the process of cell division that produces two identical daughter cells
Meiosis is the process of cell division that produces gametes (sperm and egg cells) with half the number of chromosomes
Natural selection is the process where organisms with favorable traits are more likely to survive and reproduce, as proposed by Charles Darwin
An ecosystem is a community of living organisms interacting with each other and their physical environment
The food chain shows how energy flows through an ecosystem from producers to consumers to decomposers
Producers (plants) make their own food through photosynthesis, consumers eat other organisms, and decomposers break down dead matter
The kingdoms of life are: Bacteria, Archaea, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, and Animalia
Genes are segments of DNA that code for specific proteins and determine inherited traits
A habitat is the natural environment where an organism lives and obtains what it needs to survive
An atom is the smallest unit of matter that retains the properties of an element, consisting of protons, neutrons, and electrons
The periodic table organizes all known elements by their atomic number and chemical properties
A chemical bond is a force that holds atoms together in a molecule, including ionic bonds and covalent bonds
In an ionic bond, one atom transfers electrons to another, creating charged ions that attract each other
In a covalent bond, atoms share electrons to achieve a stable electron configuration
A chemical reaction involves the rearrangement of atoms to form new substances, and must be balanced (same atoms on both sides)
pH measures how acidic or basic a solution is, on a scale from 0 (most acidic) to 14 (most basic), with 7 being neutral
Water has the chemical formula H2O, meaning two hydrogen atoms bonded to one oxygen atom
The states of matter are solid, liquid, gas, and plasma, determined by the arrangement and energy of particles
facts.query: states of matter solid liquid gas

facts.fact: Density is mass divided by volume, and determines whether an object sinks or floats in a fluid
An acid donates hydrogen ions (protons) and a base accepts them, according to the Bronsted-Lowry definition
Newton's first law of motion states that an object at rest stays at rest and an object in motion stays in motion unless acted on by a net external force (inertia)
Newton's second law states that force equals mass times acceleration (F = ma)
facts.query: Newton second law force mass acceleration

facts.fact: Newton's third law states that for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction
Energy is the capacity to do work, and it cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed (conservation of energy)
Kinetic energy is the energy of motion, calculated as one half times mass times velocity squared
Potential energy is stored energy due to position or condition, such as gravitational potential energy
Speed is distance traveled divided by time, while velocity includes both speed and direction
Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity over time
Gravity is the force of attraction between objects with mass, and on Earth accelerates objects at 9.8 meters per second squared
Waves transfer energy without transferring matter, and can be transverse or longitudinal
Ohm's law states that voltage equals current times resistance (V = IR)
The law of conservation of mass states that mass is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction
A noun is a word that names a person, place, thing, or idea
A verb expresses action or a state of being
An adjective modifies or describes a noun
An adverb modifies a verb, adjective, or other adverb, often answering how, when, where, or to what degree
A complete sentence requires at minimum a subject and a predicate (verb)
A thesis statement is a single sentence that expresses the main argument or claim of an essay
A paragraph should have a topic sentence, supporting sentences, and a concluding sentence
Active voice is when the subject performs the action, while passive voice is when the subject receives the action
A metaphor is a direct comparison stating one thing is another, while a simile uses like or as to compare
Plagiarism is presenting someone else's work or ideas as your own without proper citation
A comma separates items in a list, joins independent clauses with a conjunction, or sets off introductory phrases
A semicolon joins two closely related independent clauses without a coordinating conjunction
The three main types of literature are prose (fiction and nonfiction), poetry, and drama
facts.query: types of literature prose poetry drama

facts.fact: A protagonist is the main character of a story, and an antagonist is the character or force that opposes them
Setting in literature refers to the time and place where a story occurs
Theme is the central message or insight about life that a literary work conveys
Foreshadowing is a literary device that hints at events that will happen later in the story
Symbolism is the use of objects, characters, or actions to represent deeper meanings or ideas
Irony is a contrast between what is expected and what actually happens, including verbal, situational, and dramatic irony
Shakespeare wrote 39 plays and 154 sonnets, including Romeo and Juliet, Hamlet, and Macbeth
The American literary movement of Transcendentalism emphasized individualism, nature, and self-reliance, led by Emerson and Thoreau
The Great Gatsby by F. Scott Fitzgerald critiques the American Dream during the Jazz Age of the 1920s
The agricultural revolution (around 10,000 BCE) was when humans transitioned from hunting and gathering to farming and settling in permanent communities
Ancient Mesopotamia, located between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, is often called the cradle of civilization
Ancient Egypt developed along the Nile River and was known for pyramids, pharaohs, and hieroglyphic writing
Ancient Greece is considered the birthplace of democracy, originating in Athens around 500 BCE
The Roman Empire fell in 476 CE when the western empire collapsed, though the eastern Byzantine Empire continued until 1453
The Black Death was a bubonic plague pandemic in the 14th century that killed an estimated 25 to 50 million people in Europe
The Renaissance was a period of cultural rebirth in Europe from the 14th to 17th centuries, marked by advances in art, science, and learning
The Industrial Revolution began in Britain in the late 1700s and transformed economies from agriculture to manufacturing
World War I lasted from 1914 to 1918 and involved the Allied Powers (Britain, France, Russia, later USA) against the Central Powers (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Ottoman Empire)
World War II lasted from 1939 to 1945 and was fought between the Allies and Axis Powers, ending with Japan's surrender after atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki
The Cold War was a period of geopolitical tension between the United States and Soviet Union from 1947 to 1991, without direct military conflict between the two
The Declaration of Independence was adopted on July 4, 1776, announcing the 13 American colonies' separation from Great Britain
The US Constitution was signed in 1787 and established the framework of the federal government with three branches
The Bill of Rights is the first 10 amendments to the Constitution, protecting individual liberties like freedom of speech, religion, and press
The American Civil War lasted from 1861 to 1865 and was fought over slavery and states' rights, ending with the abolition of slavery
The Emancipation Proclamation, issued by Abraham Lincoln in 1863, declared freedom for enslaved people in Confederate states
The Louisiana Purchase in 1803 doubled the size of the United States by acquiring territory from France
The Great Depression began with the stock market crash of 1929 and lasted through the 1930s, causing massive unemployment and economic hardship
The Civil Rights Movement of the 1950s and 1960s fought against racial segregation and discrimination, led by figures like Martin Luther King Jr.
The 19th Amendment, ratified in 1920, granted women the right to vote in the United States
Pearl Harbor was attacked by Japan on December 7, 1941, leading the United States to enter World War II
The US federal government has three branches: the Legislative (Congress), Executive (President), and Judicial (Supreme Court), with checks and balances between them
Congress is the legislative branch and is divided into the Senate (100 members, 2 per state) and the House of Representatives (435 members, based on state population)
The President serves as head of the executive branch, serves 4-year terms, and can serve a maximum of 2 terms (10 years total)
The Supreme Court is the highest court in the US and has 9 justices appointed for life
The First Amendment protects freedom of speech, religion, press, assembly, and petition
Federalism is a system where power is divided between a central (federal) government and regional (state) governments
A bill becomes law by passing both houses of Congress and being signed by the President, or by a two-thirds vote overriding a presidential veto
facts.query: bill becomes law Congress President veto

facts.fact: The Electoral College elects the President, with each state having electors equal to its number of representatives plus senators
Due process, guaranteed by the 5th and 14th Amendments, means the government must follow fair legal procedures before depriving someone of life, liberty, or property
Voting in elections is both a right and a civic responsibility in a democracy
Supply and demand determine prices in a market economy: higher demand raises prices, higher supply lowers them
Scarcity is the fundamental economic problem that resources are limited but human wants are unlimited
Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative that is given up when making a choice
Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is the total value of all goods and services produced in a country in a year
Inflation is the general increase in prices over time, which decreases the purchasing power of money
A recession is a period of economic decline, typically defined as two consecutive quarters of negative GDP growth
A budget is a plan for how to spend and save income, balancing expenses against revenue
Interest is the cost of borrowing money or the return on saving money, expressed as a percentage rate
Compound interest is interest earned on both the principal amount and previously accumulated interest
The Federal Reserve is the central bank of the United States and controls monetary policy by influencing interest rates and the money supply
facts.query: Federal Reserve central bank monetary policy

facts.fact: A stock represents partial ownership in a company, and a bond is a loan to a company or government that pays interest
A computer consists of hardware (physical components) and software (programs and data)
The CPU (Central Processing Unit) is the brain of the computer that executes instructions and performs calculations
RAM (Random Access Memory) is temporary working memory that stores data while the computer is running, and is lost when power is off
A hard drive or SSD is permanent storage that retains data even when the computer is turned off
An operating system manages computer hardware and software resources and provides services for programs, examples include Windows, macOS, and Linux
The internet is a global network of interconnected computers that communicate using standardized protocols like TCP/IP
A web browser is software that retrieves and displays web pages from the internet, examples include Chrome, Firefox, and Safari
A file format determines how data is stored, such as .txt for text, .jpg for images, .mp3 for audio, and .pdf for documents
facts.query: file format txt jpg mp3 pdf

facts.fact: An algorithm is a step-by-step set of instructions to solve a problem or complete a task
Cybersecurity involves protecting computer systems and data from theft, damage, or unauthorized access using practices like strong passwords and antivirus software
Cloud computing means storing and accessing data and programs over the internet instead of on a local computer
Phishing is a type of cyber attack where scammers impersonate legitimate organizations to trick people into revealing personal information
There are seven continents: Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Australia, Europe, North America, and South America
The five oceans are the Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern, and Arctic
Latitude measures north-south position on Earth, with the equator at 0 degrees, and longitude measures east-west position, with the prime meridian at 0 degrees
A map scale shows the relationship between distances on a map and actual distances on Earth
Climate is the long-term average weather pattern of a region, while weather is the day-to-day condition of the atmosphere
The Amazon Rainforest in South America is the largest tropical rainforest in the world
The Sahara Desert in northern Africa is the largest hot desert in the world
Mount Everest in the Himalayas is the highest mountain above sea level at 8,849 meters (29,032 feet)
The Nile River in Africa is one of the longest rivers in the world at about 6,650 kilometers
A peninsula is a piece of land surrounded by water on three sides, like the state of Florida
Critical thinking involves analyzing information, questioning assumptions, evaluating evidence, and drawing reasoned conclusions
A primary source is a first-hand account or original document, while a secondary source interprets or analyzes primary sources
Fact-checking means verifying claims against reliable, independent sources before accepting them as true
Logical fallacies are errors in reasoning, such as ad hominem (attacking the person instead of the argument) or false cause (assuming correlation means causation)
facts.query: logical fallacy ad hominem false cause

facts.fact: Effective note-taking involves summarizing key points in your own words rather than copying verbatim
Time management skills include setting priorities, breaking large tasks into smaller steps, and avoiding procrastination
The scientific method involves asking a question, forming a hypothesis, testing it with an experiment, analyzing results, and drawing conclusions
An objective statement is based on facts and observable evidence, while a subjective statement is based on personal opinions or feelings
Effective communication involves clearly expressing ideas, actively listening to others, and providing constructive feedback
Citing sources gives credit to original authors and allows readers to verify your information
